mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over a 60-day horizon more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity markets.
failure_condition: Unemployment falls below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in employment and a lower unemployment rate indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both employment and unemployment improve, but S&P 500 returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting equity valuations.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate rises but S&P 500 returns remain positive over a 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests higher economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales indicates strong consumer demand, boosting corporate revenues and equity prices.
failure_condition: Retail sales growth exceeds 5% YoY but S&P 500 returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rates are high and GDP growth is strong, inflation concerns may lead to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: High federal funds rates and strong GDP growth occur, but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In an economic expansion regime, increased housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative over a 20-day horizon.
